description: Fast-drying self-levelling smoothing compound for thicknesses from 1 to 10 mm per layer
whereToUse: Ultraplan EC20 is used in interiors for levelling and smoothing differences in thicknesses from 1 to 10 mm on new or existing substrates, preparing them to receive flooring where high resistance to loads and traffic is required.
Ultraplan EC20 is especially suitable for areas subject to wheeled service loads such as chairs and trolleys (a minimum of 3 mm thickness is recommended).
Typical applications would include use in hospitals, hotels, theatres, schools and shopping centres.
Levelling concrete slabs and cementitious screeds or Mapecem, Topcem, Mapecem Pronto or Topcem Pronto based screeds
Levelling anhydrite substrates (using a suitable primer such as Primer G or Eco Prim T Plus ME
Levelling existing concrete pavements, terrazzo, ceramic, natural stone and magnesite floors
notFor: Avoid using Ultraplan EC20 for exterior levelling works, particularly when exposed to direct sunlight
Do not use Ultraplan EC20 on substrates subject to continuous rising dampness
Do not use Ultraplan EC20 on metal surfaces
Do not use Ultraplan EC20 when the temperature is below +5°C
Do not attempt to apply in large areas when the temperature is above +30°C

technicalData.label: Mixing ratio
technicalData.value: 24-25 parts of water per 100 parts by weight of Ultraplan EC20

technicalData.label: Waiting time before application of the covering: - ceramic tiles

mixing: Slowly pour a 23 kg bag of Ultraplan EC20 into a rust-free bucket containing 5.5-5.75 litres of clean potable grade water and mix with a low-speed electric mixer fitted with a suitable mixing paddle to obtain a homogeneous, self-levelling lump-free mix.
packaging: Ultraplan EC20 is available in 23 kg bags.
storage: When stored in dry conditions in the original, unopened bags, Ultraplan EC20 has a shelf life of 12 months. If stored at high temperatures and/or high humidity conditions, the shelf life may be reduced.
notes: PRODUCT NAME: the slug is 'ultraplan-eco-20' but the sheet is titled 'ULTRAPLAN EC20' and calls the product 'Ultraplan EC20' throughout; the name 'Ultraplan Eco 20' does not appear anywhere in the text. Confirm this is the intended sheet before publishing under that slug. TABLE EXTRACTION: in the reading-order text file the rows 'Mixing ratio', 'Thickness per layer' and 'Set to light foot traffic' are shuffled (it shows 'Mixing ratio: min. 3 h'); the technicalData values here follow the layout file, where Mixing ratio = 24-25 parts of water per 100 parts by weight, Thickness per layer = from 1 to 10 mm, Set to light foot traffic = min. 3 h. The rows '- resilient and carpet' and '- wood flooring' are sub-rows of 'Waiting time before application of the covering'. CONSUMPTION: one figure only (1.6 kg/m² per mm of thickness). For thicknesses greater than 10 mm (max. 20 mm) the sheet recommends adding approx. 30% by weight of 0.5 mm quartz (Quartz 0.5 ME) but gives no consumption figure for that extended mix. TEMPERATURE: the table gives an application temperature range from +5°C to +40°C while the recommendations say not to attempt large areas above +30°C. Thickness: 1 to 10 mm per layer, with a minimum of 3 mm recommended for areas subject to wheeled service loads. Primer G dilution in this sheet is 1 part Primer G with 3 parts of water (elsewhere in the same sheet '1:3 of water by volume'), which differs from the 1:1 printed in the Primer G sheet for cementitious substrates. Printing slips copied as printed: the anhydrite bullet has an unclosed bracket; the compressive strength label has a double bracket '((N/mm²)'. Water per bag (5.5-5.75 litres per 23 kg) agrees with the 24-25 parts per 100 ratio.
